newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO accuses Israel of sparking fierce clashes.
newsitem.headline: PLO accuses Israel of sparking fierce clashes.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority on Friday rejected Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's accusation that it "cynically" started and exploited violence in the West Bank and Gaza.

"The Palestinian security forces did not start the attacks, the Palestinian Authority did not violate agreements by opening the tunnel or open fire at worshippers in al-Aqsa mosque," Nabil Abu Rdainah, adviser to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, said.
"Israel carried out provocative measures such as opening the tunnel and opening fire at unarmed civilians which led to demonstrations and tension among Palestinians," he told Reuters.
PLO Executive Committee member Mahmoud Abbas, better known as Abu Mazen, accused Israel of escalating the violence that has killed 53 Palestinains and 14 Israelis in three days.
"What Israel is doing is a very dangerous escalation and has negative results," he said.
"Is using tanks and helicopters a declaration of war by Israel?" he asked.
Abbas and Abu Rdainah's comments were in response to Netanyahu's statement earlier at a news conference.
"Remember, this wasn't a spontaneous combustion. This was a deliberate political decision...it wasn't a spontaneous intifada," Netanyahu said.
Netanyahu demanded that "the Palestinian Authority commit itself immediately and in the long-term to stop the violence... return to negotiations and continue the peace process."
In Arab East Jerusalem, three Palestinian protesters were killed by Israeli police at al-Aqsa mosque.
Abbas said Arafat and his Authority were trying hard to calm the situation and salvage the peace process stalled since Netanyahu took office in June.
"But they shot worshippers in al-Aqsa mosque, this is frightening and this means Israelis are provoking Palestinians," Abbas told reporters in Gaza.
"We are commited to peace and we demand that Israel keeps its commitments and start implementing agreements," Abu Rdainah said.
PLO officials said U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher called Arafat and proposed an American-Israeli-PLO meeting soon to end the violence.
"But since Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak had invited President Arafat and Netanyahu to meet in Cairo, there could be arrangements for a four-way meeting soon," one PLO official said.
Netanyahu said he was considering Mubarak's invitation.
